stem.en: Why does artificial hybridisation involve removing the stamens from a flower and then bagging it?

text.en: To keep the petals on the flower from falling too early

feedback.en: Petals are not the concern. The method controls which pollen arrives.

text.en: So that only chosen pollen reaches the stigma

feedback.en: Yes. The flower's own pollen and outside pollen are both kept away.

text.en: To make the whole plant grow many more flowers

feedback.en: Neither step adds flowers. Both steps control pollen.

text.en: To give the seeds more food from the bag

feedback.en: A bag gives no food. It keeps unwanted pollen out.

explanation.en: Removing the stamens takes away the flower's own pollen, and the bag keeps out pollen from elsewhere. Only pollen transferred by hand then reaches the stigma.

hints.en: Which two sources of unwanted pollen are there?
Ask what each step keeps away.
